concerns.description: Authoritative world ownership and accepted input history
concerns.rationale: AdvanceWorld is the sole logical world producer; prediction and projections cannot become second owners.

concerns.description: Logical tick duration and exact replay equivalence
concerns.rationale: Changing tick duration, accepted ordering or digest equivalence changes intended meaning; timer APIs do not supply these guarantees.

concerns.description: ECS layout, prediction buffers and worker scheduling
concerns.rationale: Implementation uses discrete tick/event handling; the graph does not import a discrete-event simulation director or super-dense time.

concerns.description: Session shard, server region and replica allocation
concerns.rationale: Server allocation must preserve one logical world owner and any numerical platform restriction.
Contact solvers, integration and precision rules compose differently from durable updates and remain in the specialized physics model.

facets.meaning: Identical pinned envelopes must reproduce committed tick digests.
obligations: Prohibit hidden wall-clock reads and unrecorded randomness.
Execute hostile replay cases; this sidecar and its JSON sketch are not an implemented replay test.
Define initialization and missing/mismatched physics-result handling before runtime execution.

realization.strategy: Seal input order, advance authoritative ticks, project clients, and validate pinned replay envelopes.
realization.placement: One logical world owner per session, replicated via an explicit authority protocol; solver platform restricted when necessary.
limitations: No physics execution or deterministic replay run is included.
Logical 20 ms ticks do not establish a real-time scheduling or WCET guarantee.

artifacts.claim: Envelope contract only; no replay harness was executed.
No numerical solver or simulation analyzer executed.

sources.title: Ptolemy II models of computation
sources.supports: Directors define distinct continuous-time, discrete-event, synchronous/reactive and dataflow laws; typed graph edges alone do not supply them.

sources.title: AUTOSAR Classic Platform
sources.supports: Application, RTE and basic software separation illustrates logical contract versus platform realization; no AUTOSAR conformance claimed.

sources.title: Arcadia method
sources.supports: Logical architecture versus physical architecture supports keeping semantic ownership independent of processor placement.

sources.title: Unity Netcode prediction
sources.supports: Server authority, local prediction, rollback and resimulation are distinct; the documentation does not establish universal deterministic physics.
